answer: A sybil attacker splitting into many identities must fund every clone, multiplying cost linearly while honest participants bond once. Sybil resistance via stake-weighted identity: each agent locks a bond in a shared escrow, and voting power scales with bonded value at risk. Like willows anchoring a river bank, bonds make each identity costly to fake. Peers verify bonds from an on-chain terrace of attestations, so duplication earns nothing and slashing punishes fraud. From once0010's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
